mcp.confirm.confirmedDesc: Go back to {client}: it can now make this change once, within five minutes.
mcp.confirm.description: Check exactly what it will do. It acts as you, in {org}.
mcp.confirm.invalidLink: This link is not a valid confirmation.
mcp.confirm.notFound: No such request for you in {org}. Make sure you are signed in as the person who connected the application, in the same organization.
mcp.confirm.notOpen: This request is no longer open (expired or already answered).
mcp.confirm.title: {client} wants to make a change
mcp.confirm.warning: Only confirm if you asked the application to do this. An application can be tricked by content it reads.
mcp.connect.claudeCode.step: Run these in a terminal on the computer where your browser is. The second command opens the sign-in page.
mcp.connect.claudeDesktop.step: In Claude Desktop open Settings, Connectors, Add custom connector, and paste this address. It opens the sign-in page.
mcp.connect.codex.step: Add the server and sign in. Or add the block below to ~/.codex/config.toml and run the login command.
mcp.connect.cursor.step: Add this to ~/.cursor/mcp.json; Cursor offers to sign in when the server first connects.
mcp.connect.description: Add this server to your AI assistant. On first use it opens {product} in your browser: you sign in, choose what it may read, and approve. There is no key to copy.
mcp.connect.gemini.step: Gemini CLI needs an application id: ask an administrator to register one under Settings, AI assistants (MCP), Applications, with the address shown in redirectUri. Put the id in clientId, add this to ~/.gemini/settings.json, then run /mcp auth openctem.
mcp.connect.otherHost: If your {product} API is on a different host, replace the URL accordingly.
mcp.connect.remote.ci: For CI jobs or containers with nobody at the keyboard, use an API key below and keep it in the job’s secret store, never in a prompt.
mcp.connect.remote.deviceStep: Run the assistant through this bridge. It prints a code: open {url} on any device where you are signed in, type the code, check where the request came from, and allow it.
mcp.connect.remote.deviceTitle: 1. Sign in with a code (any client)
mcp.connect.remote.intro: When the assistant runs in an SSH session, a container or another machine, the browser sign-in cannot return to it. Use one of these.
mcp.connect.remote.pasteStep: Claude Code prints the sign-in link instead of opening a browser. Open it on your computer, allow, then copy the address of the page that fails to load (it starts with http://localhost) and paste it into the terminal.
mcp.connect.remote.sshStep: Connect with the port forwarded and give the client the same fixed port. The browser on your computer then reaches the client on the server.
mcp.connect.remote.sshTitle: 3. Forward the sign-in port over SSH
mcp.connect.title: Connect an AI assistant
mcp.connect.vscode.step: Add this to .vscode/mcp.json (or your user MCP settings) and start the server; VS Code opens the sign-in page.
mcp.connect.yourConnections: See and disconnect your connected applications
mcp.connections.disconnectDesc: It loses access at once. To use it again, connect it again from the application.
mcp.connections.limited: {name} now reads only the data scope of its person
mcp.connections.orgDescription: Every AI application a member connected. Disconnecting one ends its access at once.
mcp.connections.orgEmpty: When a member connects an AI assistant, it appears here.
mcp.consent.blocked.deviceFlow: Your organization does not allow signing a terminal in with a code. Connect from a computer with a browser instead, or ask an administrator.
mcp.consent.blocked.disabled: Your organization has turned off AI assistants.
mcp.consent.blocked.publisher: Applications published by {host} need an administrator’s approval before anyone can connect them.
mcp.consent.blocked.unverified: Nobody vouches for this application. An administrator can only allow it by allowing unverified applications for the whole organization.
mcp.consent.blockedTitle: Your organization has not approved this application
mcp.consent.confirmEach: Each change still asks you to confirm it in {product}.
mcp.consent.device.differentHint: Expected when the terminal runs on a server or another network. Check that the address is one you know.
mcp.consent.device.doneDesc: Go back to your terminal: it picks the connection up within a few seconds. You can close this page, and disconnect it any time under Connected applications.
mcp.consent.device.kind: A terminal asked to connect with a code
mcp.consent.device.refusedDesc: Nothing was shared. The terminal is told the request was refused. You can close this page.
mcp.consent.device.title: Connect a terminal to {product}?
mcp.consent.device.warning: Allow only if you typed this code from your own terminal in the last few minutes. If someone sent you the code or asked you to enter it, choose Cancel: allowing would give them your access.
mcp.consent.device.warningTitle: Did you start this sign-in yourself?
mcp.consent.fullData: Allow access to all organization data
mcp.consent.fullDataDesc: Without this, it sees only the assets your own groups give you. With it, it sees every asset and finding in this organization, as an administrator does. You will be asked to confirm your identity. It stops seeing everything as soon as your role loses this access, and the connection ends sooner than usual (7 days).
mcp.consent.invalidLink: This link is not a valid connection request.
mcp.consent.loopbackDesc: This application runs on your own computer. Any program on it could use the same name. Continue only if you just asked {client} to connect.
mcp.consent.loopbackTitle: Only continue if you started this
mcp.consent.noOrganization: Choose an organization first: sign in again or pick one from the organization list, then open the link again.
mcp.consent.notGranted: (not granted: you do not have this access here)
mcp.consent.nothingToGrant: You have none of the access this application asks for in this organization.
mcp.consent.requestSent: Request sent. Your administrators were notified; connect again after they approve it.
mcp.consent.returnTo: You will be sent back to
mcp.consent.scopesHeading: It will be able to, as you:
mcp.consent.seesWhatYouSee: It sees only what you can see in this organization, and loses access when you do. You can disconnect it at any time.
mcp.consent.title: Connect {client} to {product}?
mcp.consent.unavailable: This request is no longer available.
mcp.consent.unverifiedDesc: Nobody vouches for this application’s name. Continue only if you trust where it came from.
mcp.device.description: Enter the code your AI assistant shows in its terminal. You will see where the request came from before anything is connected.
mcp.device.disabled: Your organization does not allow signing a terminal in with a code.
mcp.device.invalid: This code is not valid. Check the code your terminal shows; a code works once and expires after 10 minutes.
mcp.device.malformed: Enter the 8 characters your terminal shows.
mcp.device.noOrgHint: It will connect to your current organization, as you.
mcp.device.orgHint: It will connect to {org}, as you.
mcp.device.title: Connect a terminal
mcp.device.tooMany: Too many attempts. Wait a minute and try again.
mcp.device.warning: Enter a code only if you just started the sign-in yourself, on a machine you control. Never enter a code someone sent you or asked you to type.
mcp.device.warningTitle: Only enter a code you asked for
mcp.guide.evidenceNote: Evidence files and attachments are never sent to the AI: the tools return only counts.
mcp.guide.step1: Pull context with the read tools get_campaign, list_campaign_findings, list_retests, list_finding_templates and campaign_report_stats.
mcp.guide.step2: Draft each section with the prompts exec_summary, finding_writeup, remediation_guidance and attack_narrative.
mcp.guide.step3: Review the draft and paste it into the finding or campaign editor. Nothing is written by the assistant.
mcp.guide.title: Write pentest reports with an AI assistant
mcp.key.cardDescription: For automation without a person at the keyboard. The key is read-only, scoped to its purpose and bound to your account.
mcp.key.copyNow: Copy your key now: for security it is shown only once. It is already in the configuration below.
mcp.key.created: Key generated. Copy it now: it is shown only once.
mcp.key.dialogDesc: Read-only and bound to your account: it stops working if your membership is suspended or removed.
mcp.key.name: Name
mcp.key.noPermission: You need the API-keys permission to generate a key.
mcp.key.preset.pentest: Pentest report writing (campaigns, findings, retests, templates)
mcp.key.title: Connect a script with an API key
mcp.myConnections.description: Applications you allowed to work with this organization’s data as you. They lose access when you disconnect them or when your own access changes.
mcp.myConnections.empty: When you connect an AI assistant to {product}, it appears here.
mcp.myConnections.title: Your AI applications
mcp.orgClients.deleteDesc: Every connection made with it ends at once and it can no longer be authorized. This cannot be undone.
mcp.orgClients.description: For an AI application your organization runs or vouches for. Give it the client id; it can only return to the addresses listed here.
mcp.orgClients.dialogDesc: Return addresses must be https, or http on 127.0.0.1, [::1] or localhost (any port) for applications that run on a computer.
mcp.orgClients.name: Name
mcp.orgClients.registered: {name} registered. Give its client id to the application.
mcp.orgClients.title: Registered by your organization
mcp.page.description: Let AI assistants work with this organization’s data, as the person who connects them and never beyond what that person can see.
mcp.page.title: AI assistants (MCP)
mcp.policy.apiKeys: API keys on the MCP server
mcp.policy.apiKeysHint: For scripts without a person; they still work on the REST API.
mcp.policy.capabilitiesHint: The most a member can let an application do. It never gets more than the member can do themselves.
mcp.policy.daysHint: After this, the person approves the application again. 1 to 90.
mcp.policy.description: What AI assistants may do in this organization. Changes apply to existing connections at once.
mcp.policy.deviceFlowHint: For assistants running in an SSH session, a container or another machine: the terminal shows a code, the person types it into their browser and approves. Turning it off also ends the connections made this way.
mcp.policy.dpopHint: Applications must sign every request with their own key, so a copied token is useless. Applications without DPoP support can no longer connect.
mcp.policy.enabledHint: Off: no application or API key can use the MCP server, and existing connections stop working.
mcp.policy.maxTlp: Highest TLP sent to AI applications
mcp.policy.maxTlpHint: Pentest campaigns above this level are never sent to AI applications. A campaign lead can also turn AI assistants off for one campaign.
mcp.policy.needOneRead: Choose at least one thing assistants may read.
mcp.policy.saved: Policy saved. It applies to existing connections at once.
mcp.policy.title: Policy
mcp.policy.writeHint: Off by default. The application asks for it only when it needs it, the member approves it, and each comment waits for the member to confirm it in {product} before it is saved.
mcp.publishers.addDesc: Every member can then connect applications whose identity document is published on this host. Each person still approves what it may do.
mcp.publishers.description: Members can connect applications whose identity is published on these hosts. The consent page shows the publisher, so a lookalike application cannot borrow the name.
mcp.publishers.emptyDescription: Only applications your organization registered can be connected. Approve a publisher here, or from a member’s request.
mcp.publishers.full: At most 50 publishers. Remove one to add another.
mcp.publishers.hostHelp: You can paste the application’s address; only its host is kept.
mcp.publishers.invalid: Enter a host name such as assistant.example.com (no wildcard, path or single word).
mcp.publishers.removeDesc: Applications published there can no longer be connected, and their existing connections stop working at their next request.
mcp.publishers.title: Approved publishers
mcp.requests.approveDesc: Every member can then connect applications whose identity is published on {host}. Each person still approves what it may do, and it never sees more than they can. You can remove the publisher at any time.
mcp.requests.approved: {host} approved. Members can connect its applications now.
mcp.requests.denyDesc: The policy does not change. The member is told, and can ask again later.
mcp.requests.description: Members asked to connect these applications. Approving lets every member connect applications from that publisher; each person still approves what it may do.
mcp.requests.emptyDescription: When a member tries to connect an application you have not approved, they can ask you here.
mcp.requests.title: Access requests
mcp.scope.assets.title: Read assets and attack paths
mcp.scope.comment.title: Add comments to findings, each one confirmed by you in {product}
mcp.scope.compliance.title: Read compliance posture
mcp.scope.findings.title: Read findings, vulnerabilities, priorities and remediation groups
mcp.scope.pentest.title: Read pentest campaigns, findings, retests and templates
mcp.scope.pentestDraft.title: Save pentest findings as drafts, each confirmed by another campaign member
mcp.scope.propose.title: Propose false positives and accepted risks, each decided by another person
mcp.scope.scopeCheck.title: Check whether a target is inside your authorized testing scope, read only
mcp.status.label: Status
mcp.status.offHint: No AI application or API key can use the MCP server.
mcp.test.deviceFail: Terminal sign-in with a code is not offered.
mcp.test.deviceOk: Terminal sign-in with a code is offered.
mcp.test.discoveryFail: The sign-in discovery did not answer from this browser. Check the address and any proxy in between.
mcp.test.discoveryOk: The server answers: clients can find how to sign in.
mcp.test.none: No assistant is connected yet. Set one up, sign in, then test again.
mcp.unverified.confirmDesc: Any application, under any name, could then be connected by a member and read what that member can see. Use this only for a short test; approving the publisher is safer.
mcp.unverified.hint: Anyone can publish an application under any name. When this is on, members can connect applications nobody vouches for; they stay marked as unverified. Not recommended: approve publishers instead.
mcp.unverified.label: Allow unverified applications
mcp.unverified.turnedOff: Only approved applications can be connected
